parameters.content:
## 4.3.2 — LinkedIn Reply-Check Polling

**Plan ID:** 4.3.2 (Phase 4 — Missing Channels + Reply Tracking)
**Sub-steps covered:** 4.3.2.1 (cron), 4.3.2.2 (LinkedIn inbox-check workaround), 4.3.2.3 (parse), 4.3.2.4 (Postgres update)

**⚠️ Tool decision not yet confirmed.** The master tracker labels 4.3.2.2 explicitly as a "(workaround)" and does not name a canonical LinkedIn-inbox-reading tool anywhere in §0.3's tool-stack table. This build uses **PhantomBuster** as a placeholder — it's the one LinkedIn-scraping tool the tracker's own reinstated tool list (§19.2) names — but this is a flagged assumption, not a confirmed decision. Swap the HTTP Request node's URL/auth if Nivy picks a different provider (or GrowChief, mentioned once at line 1802 as an alternative).

**⚠️ Built against the newer §16.4/§16.5 canonical event architecture** (communication_events, active_sequence_suppressed) rather than the simpler last_reply_channel-only pattern 4.3.1 used — see README "Note on 4.3.1" for why, and what to patch there.

**ToS note:** this is read-only inbox polling (not sending), lower risk than Module 2.1's outreach leg, but still in-scope for the Phase 7.3.1 LinkedIn automation safety review.

## ⚠️ ONE-TIME SETUP — run manually before activating

Creates the canonical §16.5 `communication_events` table (first module to actually instantiate it), the §16.4 `active_sequence_suppressed` column, the `linkedin_profile_url` column on clients_master, and this module's own dedup control table (same pattern as Module 1.1's `n8n_processed_posts`). All idempotent — safe to re-run.

parameters.jsCode:
const j = $input.item.json;
return [{ json: { ...j, alreadyProcessed: Boolean(j.message_id) } }];

parameters.query:
SELECT id, name, linkedin_profile_url,
  CASE WHEN linkedin_profile_url = $1 THEN 'profile_url' ELSE 'name' END AS match_type
FROM clients_master
WHERE linkedin_profile_url = $1
   OR lower(trim(name)) = lower(trim($2))
LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Match Lead (profile_url strong, name weak)
nodes.notes: Two-tier match per master tracker §16.5 dedup-priority spirit: exact linkedin_profile_url is strong, name-only is weak. match_type is carried through to communication_events for audit/review — see README known limitation on name-only matches.

parameters.jsCode:
const j = $input.item.json;
return [{ json: { ...j, clientFound: Boolean(j.id), clientId: j.id || null } }];

parameters.query:
UPDATE clients_master
SET last_reply_channel = 'linkedin',
    last_reply_at = $1,
    active_sequence_suppressed = true,
    linkedin_profile_url = COALESCE(linkedin_profile_url, $2),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE id = $3;

nodes.notes: Sets active_sequence_suppressed=true per §16.4 so Module 2.2 Nurture (once patched) stops the drip on real reply, not just on hardcoded status string.

nodes.name: Report to Hub
nodes.notes: S5.2 — fires in parallel off '4.3.2.4 - Update Reply Tracking + Suppress' success output, same branch as 'Insert communication_events (matched)', so the Hub round trip doesn't delay the comms-log write or the poll cycle finishing. client_id is $json.clientId (set by 'Compute Client Found Flag'; this branch only runs after 'Client Found?' is true, so never null here). odoo_lead_id resolves to null/undefined — 'Match Lead' only selects id, name, linkedin_profile_url, match_type, same not-invented pattern as 4.3.1's and 2.5's Report to Hub nodes. payload carries match_type through so a weak (name-only) match is still visible downstream in funnel_events, same audit trail Insert communication_events already keeps. NOTE: same as 4.3.1 — Hub-Dispatcher's reply.received Switch branch isn't wired yet (that's S5.4); until then this lands in funnel_events and falls through to flagged_events, same safety net as any other not-yet-consumed event type. Fires once per matched reply per poll cycle, same cardinality as the existing DB writes on this branch — no extra dedup needed beyond what 'Already Processed?' already guarantees upstream.
